subject: chemistry-hl
about: Original practice questions written for NevaIB from the IB guide's syllabus understandings and the school's unit order. Not IB past-paper questions, not publisher material and not IB markschemes: the marking points are written for self-marking. Organisms, experiments and data in data-response items are invented for practice.

choices: Loss of electrons, or an increase in oxidation state
Gain of electrons, or a decrease in the oxidation state
Gain of hydrogen, or loss of oxygen
Loss of oxygen, or a decrease in oxidation state
items.note: OIL RIG: oxidation is loss of electrons; the oxidation state increases.

items.stem: What is the oxidation state of manganese in KMnO₄?
In Zn(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Zn²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), the oxidising agent is:
items.note: The oxidising agent is reduced (gains electrons): Cu²⁺ → Cu. Zn is the reducing agent.

items.stem: In a voltaic (galvanic) cell made of Zn/Zn²⁺ and Cu/Cu²⁺ half-cells, electrons flow:
choices: From copper to zinc through the external wire
From zinc to copper through the external wire
From zinc to copper through the salt bridge
items.note: Zn is the more reactive metal: oxidised at the anode (negative electrode). Electrons go through the wire; ions move through the salt bridge.

items.stem: The purpose of the salt bridge in a voltaic cell is to:
choices: Allow ions to move and keep each half-cell electrically neutral
Allow electrons to flow between the two half-cells directly
Prevent the two metals from reacting with each other
Supply the electrons needed for reduction
items.note: The circuit is completed by ion movement in the salt bridge; electrons never pass through solutions.

items.stem: In the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, what forms at the cathode?
items.note: Cathode (negative) attracts Na⁺, which is reduced: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na. Chloride ions are oxidised to Cl₂ at the anode.

items.stem: Primary ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) heated under reflux with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI) forms:
items.note: Reflux with excess oxidant goes all the way to the carboxylic acid. Distilling off immediately gives ethanal. The colour changes orange → green.

items.stem: Using E° values (Zn²⁺/Zn −0.76 V; Cu²⁺/Cu +0.34 V), E°cell for the zinc–copper cell is:
For the cell above (n = 2, E°cell = +1.10 V, F = 96 500 C mol⁻¹), ΔG° is:
items.note: ΔG° = −nFE° = −2 × 96 500 × 1.10 = −212 300 J = −212 kJ mol⁻¹. Positive E° ↔ negative ΔG° (spontaneous).

items.stem: In the electrolysis of concentrated aqueous sodium chloride with inert electrodes, the products are:
choices: Sodium at the cathode and chlorine at the anode
Hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
Hydrogen at the cathode and chlorine at the anode
Sodium at the cathode and oxygen at the anode
items.note: Water is reduced in preference to Na⁺ (more positive E°). At high [Cl⁻], chloride is oxidised rather than water.

items.stem: To electroplate an object with silver, the object should be:
choices: The anode, in a solution containing Ag⁺ ions
The cathode, in a solution containing Ag⁺ ions
The cathode, in a solution of sodium chloride
The anode, with a silver cathode
items.note: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag deposits on the cathode. A silver anode dissolves to replace the Ag⁺.

items.stem: Deduce the balanced equation for the reaction of MnO₄⁻ with Fe²⁺ in acidic solution. Half-equations: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O; Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻.
markscheme: Electrons cancel and charges balance (+17 on each side) (1)
items.tactic: Balance electrons first, then add and cancel; check charge.

items.stem: Compare a voltaic cell and an electrolytic cell.
markscheme: Both involve oxidation at the anode and reduction at the cathode (1)
Voltaic: spontaneous reaction converts chemical energy to electrical energy (1)
Electrolytic: electrical energy drives a non-spontaneous reaction (1)
Voltaic anode is negative; electrolytic anode is positive (1)
items.tactic: Compare: one similarity plus paired differences.

items.stem: A cell is made from Ag⁺/Ag (E° = +0.80 V) and Cu²⁺/Cu (E° = +0.34 V). (a) Identify the anode and cathode. (b) Write the overall equation. (c) Calculate E°cell and state what it shows.
markscheme: (a) Cu is the anode (oxidised); Ag is the cathode (1)
Positive, so the reaction is spontaneous (ΔG° negative) (1)
items.tactic: The more positive E° half-cell is reduced. Do not multiply E° by stoichiometric coefficients.

items.stem:
(Invented data for practice.) A student measured the voltage between copper (in 1 mol dm⁻³ Cu²⁺) and four invented metals in their 1 mol dm⁻³ ion solutions: metal P 0.78 V (P negative); Q 1.45 V (Q negative); R 0.12 V (R positive); S 0.40 V (S negative).
(a) Arrange P, Q, R, S and Cu in order of reducing strength (strongest first). (b) Predict the voltage of a P–Q cell and which is negative. (c) State why the measured values may differ from data booklet values.
markscheme: (c) Non-standard conditions, e.g. temperature, concentration, or resistance/impure metal surfaces (1)
Order justified: larger voltage with the metal negative = more reactive (1)
items.tactic: Unfamiliar context: find the syllabus idea being tested, quote the data (with units) when you describe a trend, then explain it with that idea. One marking point per linked step.
